Thanks for the ping, Jonas.

High level position: we do want to remove text-embed-v1 from the catalog for two reasons — ongoing maintenance cost and improved quality/size trade-offs in the v2 series — but we also want a low-friction path for enterprise customers who need extra runway. Proposed approach below.

Proposal (product-stoplight):
- Public EoL announcement: Jan 15, 2027 (docs + dashboard flag).
- Default public cutover: Mar 1, 2027 (60 days after announcement).
- Customer exception path: 60-day enterprise extension (starts Mar 1) + optional paid 30-day bridge (if customer needs full 90 days).
- Compatibility bridge: a lightweight compatibility shim that accepts v1 calls and proxies to v2 with a transform layer that normalizes embeddings (adds minimal CPU work). Not all semantic differences can be hidden, but this preserves vector dims and offers a migration scorecard.

Product asks if we greenlight the exception lane:
1) Marketing: one customer-facing FAQ and an internal notice for CS & AE (2–3 bullets + example curl).
2) Docs: a migration runbook and quick test harness with sample vectors and expected thresholds.
3) Evals: surface a short A/B check comparing v1->v2 mapped vectors for customer verification.

I'll draft the external comms template and the internal CS FAQ. I attached a starter timeline spreadsheet — plz add infra estimates and legal if needed.

Marissa
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

Thanks — here's the infra reality and risk profile.

Feasibility notes:
- Compatibility shim: doable as a request-time transform layer for text-embed calls. It will add ~20–40ms p99 in the common path depending on batch sizes and will slightly increase GPU to CPU handoff.
- KV/cache: for similarity services that rely on cached vectors we recommend a two-step migration: (1) run a background remap job to regenerate vectors on v2, (2) run a short parallel-read window where requests read both versions and gradually switch traffic. That avoids reindex storms.
- Cost/SLO: if we offer a 90-day paid bridge we should require reserved capacity to avoid noisy-neighbor effects. Expected billable uplift ~8–12% for a mid-sized account under this plan.

Operational asks for an exception:
- Sales: confirm whether Acme will accept a paid bridge or needs a free extension (Ben).
- CS: coordinate a tech-runbook and customer A/B checklist (Laura).
- Engineering: we'll need a short 2-week sprint to build the shim, plus 1 week of integration and QA. Target ship: Feb 22, 2027 to support a Mar 1 soft-cutover.

I'll put a small capacity reservation template together and a basic rollback plan.

Rishi
Head of Serving Runtime
